claim: Since the 1997 rewrite (sales after May 6, 1997), up to $250,000 of gain on a main home is tax-free for a single filer and $500,000 for most joint filers; the dollar amounts have never been adjusted. $250,000 in 1997 prices is about $512,494 in prices of the 12 months to August 2026, and the limit fell from 1.72 times the median new-home price (1997) to 0.61 times (2026 Q2). Take a home bought at the national median new-home sales price in a given quarter and grow its value with a national repeat-sales home price index to June 2026: the gain exceeds $250,000 for purchases in 107 of the 158 quarters from 1987 Q1 to 2026 Q2 - every quarter from 1987 through 2005 Q1 and from 2008 Q4 through 2017 Q1. A median home bought in 1997 Q3 shows a gain of about $421,964; a single seller (never married, divorced, or widowed more than 2 years earlier) would owe tax on about $171,964, about $25,795 at the 15% long-term rate, while a married couple owes nothing (no quarter's gain exceeds $500,000; maximum about $439,615). Bought 2000 Q1: gain about $387,451. Sources: 26 U.S.C. 121(b); FRED MSPUS, CSUSHPINSA, CPIAUCSL. Tax year 2026 rules.

numbers.definition: For each quarter q with MSPUS (median sales price of new houses sold, quarterly) and all 3 monthly CSUSHPINSA values: gain(q) = MSPUS(q) x (CSUSHPINSA latest month / mean of CSUSHPINSA over the 3 months of q - 1). Year of the latest q with gain > 250,000.
Quarter number of that latest q.
Number of quarters q with gain(q) > 500,000.
Number of quarters q with gain(q) > 250,000.
Number of quarters q for which gain(q) is defined (1987 Q1 - 2026 Q2).
Maximum gain(q) over all quarters, rounded.
250000 x (mean of last 12 monthly CPIAUCSL values, Sep 2025-Aug 2026) / (mean of the 12 monthly values of 1997), rounded.
250000 / mean of the 4 quarterly MSPUS values of 1997, 2 decimals.

assumptions: Purchase price = national median sales price of new houses sold in the purchase quarter; value today = purchase price x change in the national repeat-sales index (quarter mean to June 2026).
Gain = value today minus purchase price: no improvements added to basis, no selling costs, no depreciation; seller meets the 2-of-5-year ownership and use tests.
Single seller = unmarried filer (including divorced, or widowed more than 2 years before the sale); joint sellers get $500,000.
Tax illustration uses the 15% long-term rate only (ignores the 0%/20% brackets, the 3.8% net investment income tax and state tax).
